beliefs.practice: Read the DocumentDB/Mongo connection string only from an environment variable (DOCUMENTDB_URI) or a secrets provider at runtime; never commit credentials, connection strings, or API keys to source control or plaintext files.

Use a single, long-lived MongoClient (connection pool) instance per process (create it at app startup and reuse it for all requests) instead of creating a new client per request; close it cleanly on shutdown.

Enable TLS/SSL for connections and validate server certificates (use secure=true / tls=true options), and restrict access with network controls (VNet/private endpoint or IP firewall) rather than relying solely on username/password.
Store cached branch summaries as one document per branch with a unique index on branch_id so you can maintain/refresh a branch summary using updateOne(..., upsert=True) targeted by branch_id.

Create a TTL index on the branch_summaries collection (or on a last_refreshed field) when you want automatic expiry of rolled-up caches, and set retention by expireAfterSeconds so stale summaries are removed automatically.

For the transactions collection, create compound indexes that match the $match stage of the aggregation pipelines (e.g., { branch_id: 1, transaction_date: 1 } and any other frequently filtered fields) so aggregation can use indexes before $facet.
Push restrictive $match and $project stages as early as possible in aggregation pipelines and include only the fields needed by subsequent stages to reduce memory and CPU during $facet and grouping.

When running heavy aggregation pipelines, set allowDiskUse=True (or the driver equivalent) and test with explain() to ensure operations won't be rejected for memory; use paged or incremental refresh for very large datasets.
Use explain() and the cluster's MCP/monitoring tools to inspect query and aggregation plans and verify which indexes are used; record and act on any COLLSCAN warnings before shipping.

Implement retries with exponential backoff for transient network errors and rate-limiting responses; prefer idempotent operations (upsert) or include a retry token for non-idempotent operations to avoid duplicates.

Enable retryableWrites and retryReads on the Mongo client when supported, and set reasonable serverSelectionTimeoutMS/connectTimeoutMS so the app fails fast during misconfiguration instead of hanging.

For the cached summaries refresh job, perform an atomic upsert per branch (updateOne with filter on branch_id and upsert:true) so refreshes are safe if retried or interrupted; avoid multi-document partial updates unless wrapped in a transaction.

If you need to update multiple documents atomically (e.g., update summary and a related metadata doc), use multi-document transactions only when necessary and test latency/throughput impact; prefer single-document design to avoid transactions when possible.

Create an index on fields used for top-N queries or sorts in the dashboard (e.g., { branch_id: 1, avg_ticket: -1 }) to avoid in-memory sorts and speed up list endpoints that order by metrics in branch_summaries.

If using vector search over embeddings, store embeddings as numeric arrays and create the cluster-provided vector index (DiskANN/HNSW/IVF) with matching dimension, metric (cosine/L2), and maxDimensions; test retrieval latency and recall on representative data.

Keep OpenAI (or other LLM) API keys out of the repository and environment files committed to source control; require OPENAI_API_KEY at runtime or provide a clear no-op fallback in tests and CI so the app doesn't accidentally call external APIs during verification.

Rate-limit and validate user inputs to the /refresh and /ask endpoints (authenticate/authorize refresh operations) to avoid accidental large refresh jobs or prompting expensive vector/LLM queries from untrusted callers.

Monitor collection-level metrics, RU/compute usage, latency and throttling in the cloud console (or MCP tools), and add alerts for sustained high CPU/IO or throttling so you can scale the cluster or optimize indexes before dashboards degrade.
